# Velair 1.8.0-beta.1

Velair 1.8.0-beta.1 is a beta release intended for real-world testing before Velair 1.8.0. It adds a complete single-climate Lovelace experience, expands
Comfort into useful environmental context, and makes climate control easier to
integrate and diagnose while preserving existing configurations.

## ✨ Added

- Added mode-only blocks that change the HVAC mode without sending a target temperature, including `auto`, across schedules, profiles, and templates ([#29](https://github.com/cgonfer/velair/issues/29)). Their compact Target control can disable or restore the temperature input without adding another mobile column, and the public `velair.set_hvac_mode` service exposes the same Velair-owned intent to scripts and automations.
- Added a responsive, theme-aware single-climate Lovelace card that brings together a compact semantic header, configurable Current state, timeline, Room Assist and Preconditioning sections, Automatic/Manual ownership, HVAC mode and setpoint controls, native Home Assistant shortcuts, and reorderable Boost, Pause, and script actions. Its editor, collapsible views, menus, feedback, overflow controls, and touch interactions adapt across mobile, tablet, and desktop.
- Added an expanded, observational Comfort model with Simple rectangular, Guided psychrometric, and Custom temperature-aware humidity ranges, plus Humidex, dew point, and absolute humidity readings selected from one Velair-or-Home-Assistant source control. Guided adapts one midpoint reference range into a temperature-dependent curve, while Custom retains direct endpoint control; the graph follows the selected model and the compact, collapsible configuration separates data sources, model, preferences, outdoor comparison, and additional metrics. Physical Environmental condition remains the primary color-coded status, with a separate Humidex indicator when perceived heat disagrees. One backend interpretation is reused across the panel, climate card, API, Diagnostics, events, range summaries, and cautious ventilation context without changing climate control, while a new per-zone Ventilation opportunity sensor exposes six conservative states for automations: unavailable, no opportunity, may help, comfort possible, trade-off, and already comfortable.
- Added per-zone control and optional delivery diagnostics entities so dashboards and automations can identify Velair ownership and inspect whether climate commands succeeded, failed, retried, or could not be delivered ([#22](https://github.com/cgonfer/velair/pull/22), [#26](https://github.com/cgonfer/velair/discussions/26)).
- Added a persisted target-temperature step fallback for climate entities that omit `target_temp_step`. Velair remembers the latest valid reported step, anchors target grids to the climate minimum, and applies the effective value consistently across schedules, profiles, Room Assist, imports, climate-card controls, restarts, and Celsius/Fahrenheit migrations.

## 🚀 Improved

- Standardized contextual information controls across Velair with accessible, theme-aware sizing and viewport-safe help on mouse, keyboard, and touch interfaces.

## 🛠️ Fixed

- Fixed delayed, intermediate, and out-of-order climate updates being mistaken for manual adjustments, preventing affected climates from unexpectedly leaving Automatic control or entering Keep automatic reapply loops ([#28](https://github.com/cgonfer/velair/issues/28)).
- Fixed hidden Room Assist help content creating an empty horizontal area at the end of the temperature graph for some target combinations.
- Fixed a Home Assistant thread-safety error that could prevent Velair from restoring the current climate intent when an unavailable entity reconnects ([#27](https://github.com/cgonfer/velair/issues/27)).

## 🧭 Notes

- Velair 1.8.0-beta.1 introduces no intentional breaking changes. Existing configurations remain compatible, stored data is migrated automatically, and all new Comfort sources and climate-card sections are optional.
- The existing Environmental condition state remains compatible with current automations while its attributes and related events expose the new Comfort context.
- Delivery diagnostics entities are optional and disabled by default.
- A new [Velair Sensor Reference](https://github.com/cgonfer/velair/blob/main/docs/user/sensors.md) documents every Velair sensor, what each one includes, and practical examples for dashboards and automations.
- Outdoor Comfort comparisons use current readings and do not account for rain, wind, outdoor air quality, security, window state, forecasts, or the actual rate of air exchange. They provide context only and never operate windows or change climate control.
- After updating through HACS, restart Home Assistant and refresh the browser or companion app. If an older interface remains visible, perform a hard refresh or clear the site cache.
